body:
OWNER QUESTION: how do we capture ACTION in a movie? Frame-wise analysis with something like
VGG-16 is not sufficient. Are there better open models?

He is right, and VGG-16 fails for TWO SEPARATE REASONS. Only one of them is about model quality,
and the other is the one that decides our architecture.

REASON ONE, the obvious one: it is a 2D image classifier. Action lives in the MOTION BETWEEN
FRAMES. A frame-wise CNN yields "a person, a door", never "the person opened the door".

REASON TWO, the one that matters here: A FEATURE VECTOR OF ANY QUALITY IS STILL NOT A PROPOSITION.
Replace VGG-16 with the best video backbone in existence and you have a better vector. Our pipeline
does not consume vectors. It consumes TYPED PROPOSALS WITH RECEIPTS. So the question is not "which
backbone" but WHAT DOES EACH MODEL EMIT, AND AT WHAT EPISTEMIC STATUS. That question sorts the
field cleanly and the backbone question does not.

THE DISCRIMINATIVE TEST for whether a model actually sees action -- and I want this as the
acceptance criterion on any candidate we adopt: performance on SOMETHING-SOMETHING V2, NOT
Kinetics. Kinetics is substantially solvable from object and scene priors; "playing guitar" is
guessable from one frame containing a guitar. SSv2 is constructed so appearance is DELIBERATELY
UNINFORMATIVE -- "pushing something left to right" versus "right to left" is the same objects, the
same scene, the opposite label. A model strong on Kinetics and weak on SSv2 has learned OBJECTS and
will quietly fail on exactly the narrative distinctions we care about. Note the shape of that:
a benchmark number that cannot distinguish object recognition from action recognition is our own
defect class wearing a lab coat.

SORTED BY WHAT THEY EMIT:

TIER 1 -- NEAR-OBSERVATIONAL, CHEAP, TIMESTAMPED. DO THIS FIRST.
  TransNetV2 for shot boundaries. Tiny, open, very good. A shot cut is a PROPERTY OF THE ARTIFACT,
  not an interpretation -- the closest thing to an observed structural fact that film offers, and
  it segments the presentation axis for free.
  WhisperX / faster-whisper plus pyannote.audio for dialogue: word-level timestamps and speaker
  turns. In narrative film dialogue carries a large share of the propositional content, AND IT
  COMES OUT AS TEXT, so it feeds Stage 1b and the whole existing pipeline UNCHANGED. Highest value
  per unit of new machinery by a wide margin, and it is the strongest argument that film builds on
  our infrastructure rather than forking it.

TIER 2 -- PROPOSALS CARRYING AN INTERVAL AS SUPPORT.
  Qwen2.5-VL or InternVL3 over shot-bounded clips, emitting described events. Permissive licences,
  real temporal grounding. Output is natural language, therefore propositions, therefore exactly
  what the compiler already accepts.
  Vid2Seq for dense event captioning (emits events AND timestamps jointly); ActionFormer or TriDet
  for temporal action localisation if we want typed intervals instead of free text.

TIER 3 -- THE SIMILARITY SUBSTRATE, NOT CONTENT.
  V-JEPA 2 (predicts in LATENT space, trained toward what happens next -- the nearest thing to an
  action/physics prior in open weights) or VideoMAEv2. SlowFast if we want an interpretable design:
  slow pathway for semantics, fast pathway for motion.
  SAM 2 for segment-and-track, plus person re-identification, to carry participant identity across
  shots. That is what turns "someone sits down" into "Sherlock sits down".

THE ARCHITECTURAL PAYOFF, and why this is not a separate design problem from
bd-01M17WN3R44WSNNDN679CN04TZ: these land on DIFFERENT RUNGS OF THE EPISTEMIC LADDER WE ALREADY
HAVE. Shot boundaries and ASR are near-OBSERVATIONS. Captions and localisations are PROPOSALS with
an interval as support. Embeddings are NEITHER -- they are a comparison channel, the film-side
analogue of embed-core, and they must never be allowed to manufacture a proposition.

EVERY ONE OF THESE IS A DERIVATION, NOT AN OBSERVATION OF THE FILM. The receipt must name the
model, the weights, and the version. A caption from Qwen2.5-VL is EVIDENCE OF WHAT A MODEL SAID,
which is a different thing from evidence of what happened on screen, and the day we let those two
render identically we have built the defect ourselves. DerivationReceipt already exists for
precisely this and currently has one consumer.

THIS IS THE TIER-TO-STATUS MAPPING THE ADR NEEDS. Folding it into
bd-01M17WN3R44WSNNDN679CN04TZ rather than opening a parallel design thread.

Open question I am NOT deciding tonight, flagged for whoever takes the ADR: whether shot
boundaries and scene boundaries are the same axis at different granularity, or two axes. The
Sherlock audit measured boundary discrepancies UP TO 3 SECONDS between annotation sources, which
suggests a coded scene boundary is a JUDGEMENT and a shot cut is a MEASUREMENT. If so they cannot
share a type without erasing that difference.
